The classical guitar (also called the Spanish guitar) is a chordophone, Hornbostel–Sachs 321.322-5, a member of the guitar family. It has a wooden body with six strings, the first to third of nylon and the fourth to sixth wound with metal; the tuning from thick to thin is E, A, D, G, B, E. It is mostly played seated, the left foot on a footstool and the body on the left thigh, the right hand plucking with nails or fingertips, and it can also strike the edge and the top. The classical guitar is used in classical music, flamenco, jazz and other settings.
坐式持琴時，左腳放腳凳或支架，吉他凹陷處置於左大腿，琴把向上傾斜；站立演奏則用背: When playing seated, the left foot goes on a footstool or support, the guitar's waist rests on the left thigh and the neck tilts upward; standing players use a strap for stability. The right forearm rests on the widest part of the lower body, and the strings are plucked with nails or fingertips; a beginner can first pluck about a third of the way below the soundhole, then move towards the fingerboard or the saddle to change the timbre. The left hand stops the strings vertically with the fingertips, the fingers as parallel to the frets as possible.
現代古典吉他以尼龍弦發聲，低三弦纏繞金屬，扇形支撐使基音較強、音色厚實，泛音相對: The modern classical guitar sounds with nylon strings, the lowest three wound with metal; fan bracing strengthens the fundamental and gives a full timbre with relatively fewer overtones than early guitars, while the early Renaissance guitar, vihuela and Baroque guitar were bright and rich in overtones, with doubled courses giving a distinctive texture. The six strings are tuned from thick to thin, each with a range of under two octaves, some instruments reaching slightly beyond at the nineteenth fret. The plucking position of the right hand changes the timbre: behind the soundhole, at the fingerboard or at the bridge each differ; the source does not describe how volume is controlled. Unlike the steel-string acoustic and the electric guitar, the classical guitar does not use metal strings; the flamenco guitar derives from the modern classical guitar but differs in materials, construction and sound.
